title: Tesla Launches Production Cybercab Robotaxi in Austin
summary: Tesla revealed the production Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel, in Austin on September 3, sending shares up about 5% as the autonomy bet returns to focus.
body_markdown:
Gotrade News - Tesla unveiled its production Cybercab robotaxi at a launch event in Austin, Texas on September 3, sending shares up about 5% to around $376. The two-seat vehicle has no steering wheel or pedals and runs entirely on Full Self-Driving software, putting Tesla's autonomy bet back at the center of the stock's story.


According to[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/03/tesla-officially-launches-the-cybercab-2-things-investors-need-to-know/) , the reveal is a milestone for[Tesla (TSLA)](https://www.heygotrade.com/en/us-stock/tsla/) , but it is a product launch rather than a regulatory green light, and much of the robotaxi upside is already built into the price.


## Key Takeaways


- Tesla revealed the production Cybercab, a two-seat robotaxi with no steering wheel or pedals, in Austin on September 3.
- Tesla stock rose about 5% to roughly $376 as investors refocused on the autonomy story.
- The event was an unveiling, not a federal safety approval, so how fast the service scales still depends on regulators.


## A Two-Seat Robotaxi With No Steering Wheel


The Cybercab is Tesla's first vehicle designed purely for autonomy, navigating with cameras and artificial intelligence rather than a human driver. Per[The Motley Fool](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/03/tesla-officially-launches-the-cybercab-2-things-investors-need-to-know/) , Tesla had already added 45 Cybercabs to its Austin network ahead of the event, and reporting suggests riders in the city could begin hailing one through the existing Robotaxi app as early as the following week.
